  • 受访：袁培笙
  • 访谈：路行己

访谈背景：从 1997 年到 2000 年初，上海育碧的研发线路主要分为两条。一条以《分裂细胞》为代表，另一条则以《幽灵行动》为代表，这两条研发线最终汇聚到《分裂细胞 4 双面间谍》。本次我与曾经负责《幽灵行动》系列的袁培笙老师进行了远程访谈，一起回顾了上海育碧从 1998 年《雷曼 2》到《细胞分裂 4》这段开启国产 AAA 游戏之路的历史。

访谈时间：2026 年 6 月 4 日

扁平化团队与影视工业化

行己：袁老师，能否介绍一下您是何时加入上海育碧的？

袁老师：上海育碧是 96 年进入中国的，最初建立了发行部门，主要是把海外游戏代理到国内销售。在这个过程中育碧很快发现中国有很多具有潜力的优秀开发人才。因此开始组建研发团队。大约在 98 年的时候，我得知育碧在上海开设了游戏开发部门，于是同年 7 月份面试通过，便进入了上海育碧。我当时是个非常懵懂的状态，因为专业不对口，就选择了面试 Tester（游戏测试）的职位。没想到去的时候，面试了整整半天。当时我觉得面试个测试职位怎么什么都考，又考数学，又考物理，又考编程。面试编程题目的时候，我告诉面试官我不是计算机专业的，他们就让我用比较抽象的方法去解答一些逻辑问题，提出算法。印象最深的是到最后育碧还会考察游戏水平，让我跟公司的同事打了好几把游戏。

行己：育碧当时对测试的要求都这么高吗？

袁老师：其实这些要求跟育碧的人才培养计划有很大关系。虽然招聘的时候有测试员、策划、项目经理等各种岗位需求，但是育碧录用时更多考虑的是这个人才的实际潜力，也就是说被招进来的员工会根据他的实际表现来安排岗位。另外一个特点是当时在育碧看来，所有的岗位都只是工作分工不同，例如：项目经理在传统认知里是个高级岗位，大家需要听他的话，但是在早期的育碧不是这样的，管理岗位只是一个职位分工。大家完全可以主动跟自己的上司要求去尝试一些自己认为更适合的工作。

行己：能否介绍一下您在育碧参与的第一个项目？

袁老师：当时育碧有两个项目，一个是《摩纳哥 GP》的 F1 项目（参见沈黎老师访谈）。另一个是《雷曼 2》的 PS 移植项目，我参与的就是《雷曼 2》的移植项目。由于当时 PS 的机能已经落后 PC 很多了，因此《雷曼 2》的移植难度非常高。我记得项目团队为了能让游戏在 PS 上流畅运行，不光做了大量的模型和贴图优化，连音效都优化了。说起来那时候公司的职业发展空间也非常大，我在测试部门仅入职了 2 周，就以 Level Designer 的职位加入了雷曼 2 项目。当时我们使用的是叫做 CPA 的自研游戏引擎（编辑器），它有一些窗口，你可以通过编写脚本来控制游戏里的角色和道具。

笔者按：CPA 引擎（Common Programming Architecture），1997 年左右育碧为了开发新一代 3D 游戏，投入约 50 人团队开发全新的 3D 引擎。最早用于《Tonic Trouble》随后用于《雷曼 2》。

袁老师：我在《雷曼 2》工作了三个月后，紧接着公司就启动了一个和德国积木品牌 Play Mobile 合作的项目。它是一种跟乐高很像的拼搭玩具，里面包含了大量中世纪题材的内容。我作为 Level Designer 加入了这个项目，不过没过多久，公司就换了方向，开始和迪士尼合作开发一款唐老鸭的 PS 平台跳跃类游戏，叫《Donald Duck: Quack Attack》。这部作品采用了和《雷曼 2》一样的 CPA 引擎，但是在玩法设计上其实更接近《古惑狼》。这个项目的关卡设计是上海育碧独立完成的，当时我们为了便于参考，有同学特意购买了《古惑狼》的 1-3 合集，不过是盗版的。因为这个盗版游戏还出过一个小插曲，有一次同事玩完后没有收好，被当时的工作室老板 Gilles 路过看到了，他愤怒的拿起光盘说，我们公司不允许出现盗版盘，这是谁的？！话说回来，《Donald Duck: Quack Attack》也是我们首次使用理性关卡设计（Rational Level Design）的作品，我也在这个项目中成为了关卡组长。 不过现在回看，感觉这个项目还略显稚嫩，毕竟是我们独立完成的第一个项目。好在还有唐老鸭的 IP 加持，据说销量也还不错。

行己：您在这个项目之后就参与了《幽灵行动》吗？

袁老师：在《Donald Duck: Quack Attack》之后，我们实际上又开发了一个类似互动式电影的项目。这是上海育碧最早制作的 PS2 项目之一，应该也是国内最早制作的 PS2 项目。我还记得当时 PS2 有出口限制，我们还做了特殊申请才将游戏机和 Kit（开发机）弄到上海。所以我们应该也是国内第一批玩上 PS2 的玩家吧（笑）。

笔者按：PS2 于 2000 年 3 月 4 日在日本发售，日本通产省（MITI）一度将 PS2 纳入出口管制范围。原因是 PS2 的 Emotion Engine 处理器和 MagicGate 加密技术被认为具有潜在的军民两用性质，需要申请出口许可。甚至有媒体报道称其图形处理能力理论上可用于导弹制导或高性能计算。不过这个限制持续时间并不长，2000 年 4 月日本政府很快放宽了相关规定。

袁老师：这个项目是我们和一位著名的华裔导演合作开发的。为了在游戏中展现出电影级的视觉效果，我们还把很多用在影视行业的技术应用到了游戏开发中。例如，所有角色的动作几乎都是通过动作捕捉完成的。大约到 2001 年中，项目本身推进非常艰难，育碧总部也对互动电影这个方向出现了动摇，导致这个项目的项目经理承受了极大压力，后来这位项目经理离职了，我就从关卡组长成为了这个项目的项目经理，把产品最终做完。

行己：这个项目最后怎么样了？

袁老师：最后还是被总部关掉了（笑）。不过我认为这个项目被关掉的深层原因是育碧当时的战略方向出现了变化。

红色风暴来袭

《幽灵行动》PS2 版
袁老师收藏

行己：育碧的战略方向发生了什么变化？

袁老师：2000 年的时候育碧收购了汤姆克兰西（Tom Clancy）的 Red Storm（红色风暴）工作室。通过这次收购，育碧不仅获得了《彩虹六号》、《幽灵行动》这两大游戏品牌，还拥有了汤姆克兰西这个硬核军事系列的冠名权。可以说这次收购打开了育碧进入硬核军事游戏的大门，也为后来的《细胞分裂》系列打下了基础。话说回来，随着这次收购的完成，上海育碧的重心开始转向硬核军事游戏的 PS2 移植。这其中主要包含两个主线，一个是沈黎老师他们负责的《细胞分裂》，另一个就是我们负责的《幽灵行动》。

笔者按：虽然两部游戏都是在育碧完成收购之后推出的，但《幽灵行动》是 Red Storm 在被收购前正在开发的作品，而《细胞分裂》则是育碧在完成收购后基于其内部项目《The Drift》原创的系列。

袁老师：我在加入《幽灵行动》的时候还不是正式的制作人，因为这个项目当时在育碧内部非常重视，所以它刚启动的时候，制作人是当时上海育碧的总研发负责人翁颖明‌先生。翁前辈是我的良师益友，我刚进入测试部门的时候他就是我的领导，当时他让我去玩各种游戏，然后给他写心得，这使我在游戏设计能力方面有了很大成长。不过在《幽灵行动》开始不久之后翁先生就离开了，所以我就接任了这个项目的项目经理（Project Manager）。随后，育碧就开始推广制作人的管理模式从项目管理升级到对游戏全面负责，包括不限于内容、人员、预算等等。我也就是在这个时候成为了《幽灵行动》的制作人的。

笔者按：翁颖明‌老师是上海育碧的第一位中方员工，后来在 EA 中国和神游科技担任重要职位，属于中国游戏发展历史上的重要贡献者之一。

行己：《幽灵行动》是使用什么引擎开发的？

袁老师：《幽灵行动》使用的是 Red Storm 自研的同名引擎。我记得当时为了熟悉这个引擎，我们还同时开发了另一个游戏来试水。这个游戏叫《The Sum of All Fears》（恐惧总和）。这部游戏也改编自汤姆克兰西的同名作品，当时还推出了电影。《幽灵行动》（PS2 版）和这个游戏不仅使用了同一个引擎，甚至很多底层的素材和代码都是共用的。在《The Sum of All Fears》项目中有一件事让我印象深刻，有一个周日下午我一个人来到公司检查《The Sum of All Fears》的开发版本，准备周一的 Check List。当时正好碰到一个来送快递的小哥，于是我就请他玩了一会儿这个游戏，想让他给我们提提意见。结果他当时玩的非常开心，甚至还发现了很多我都没注意过的细节（笑）。这点非常令人意外，我想可能是因为我们每天都在反复体验这个游戏，所以都有点麻木了。但当这个快递小哥玩的时候，他玩的很兴奋，这确实给我打了一个很大的强心针。因为在 2000 年左右，硬核军事游戏甚至对上海团队中的大多数人来说也是个很小众的游戏类型，甚至自己都有点迷茫这种游戏究竟好玩在哪。这次误打误撞遇到了目标玩家，这可以说是我后来重视目标用户反馈的开端。

《The Sum of All Fears》PS2 版
袁老师收藏

行己：《幽灵行动》是在这个游戏完成之后开始制作的吗？

袁老师：没有，这两个游戏几乎是平行进行的，而且《幽灵行动》与《The Sum of All Fears》不同，他是我们做的第一个开放世界射击游戏，最终销量超过了百万（194 万，来源：VGChartz）。

行己：这个项目中有什么令您印象深刻的事情么？

袁老师：《幽灵行动》最令我印象深刻的应该就是我们在 UI 上加入了目标指示器。这是 PS2 版独有的，而且形成了专业编辑和玩家完全相反的口碑评价。这个设计的起源来自一次游戏店里的调研。当时我带着一张《幽灵行动》早期版本去游戏店里找玩家测试，想看看玩家的反应，结果大家玩的鸦雀无声。那个时候玩家还基本没有接触过开放世界游戏，对于接下来要做什么，目标在哪里完全没有认识，结果我只能灰溜溜的把盘带走了。回到公司以后，我们就认为游戏还是需要给没有接触过开放世界的玩家提供一个指引，于是就在游戏的小地图上增加了一个指引目标的箭头。不过这个设计被 IGN 批评了，因为他们觉得这游戏的核心体验就应该是在开放世界里自由探索的乐趣。而我们加了指引以后，反而让他们觉得没意思了。这种和编辑之间的想法对立也让我第一次感受到文化和生活的差异对游戏设计的影响。因为对于很多欧美人来说，他们在生活中是比较容易接触到枪械的，也有去野外打猎的爱好，因此在开放世界中自主寻找目标的体验是他们的一种生活乐趣，而这种体验在亚洲国家其实是很少的，亚洲的生活状态更强调目标感。

笔者按：这个案例反映出市场销售中“沉默的大多数现象”，在当时的游戏市场中，由于 PS 主打泛用户市场，因此很多 PS 玩家往往不具备丰富的游戏经历和高超的游戏技巧，这些玩家虽然是 PS 的主流玩家，但他们的声音在当时很难被游戏开发者知道，而媒体编辑由于拥有更好的沟通渠道，因此更容易发声，但他们没能代表当时 PS 上的大部分玩家。这也是后来为何出现游戏评分与玩家口碑两极分化的核心原因之一：编辑个人的偏好无法代表大多数玩家的需求。

袁老师：还有一个令我印象非常深刻的是我们游戏有一次母盘的送审事故。当时因为《幽灵行动》与《The Sum of All Fears》是同时开发的，使用的引擎也一样，因此这两个游戏都是一个小组开发的。这就使得团队需要同时维护两套游戏数据，大家经常需要切换思路，非常痛苦，开发时间也非常有限，导致连给 SONY 提交母盘的时间都被用掉了。当时国际快递送到欧洲总部大概需要一周时间，我们把这一周都给用完了，经过连续通宵的加班，我们直到提交版本的最后一天才把游戏的母盘压出来。比较幸运的是当时我们的研发总监是从法国派过来的，他为了给我们争取时间特意把回法国的时间拖到了压盘完成的最后一天，然后他直接坐飞机给我们把盘送到了法国。那天晚上我在路边吃麻辣烫的时候，我们老板 Corinne 打电话过来很生气的告诉我那个版本已经被拒掉了。研发总监阿诺德白跑一趟，然后他就直接把电话挂了。当时我真是吓得一身冷汗，都不知道出了什么问题。第二天，阿诺德直接从法国飞回来，脸色铁青的回到了办公室。他说：“我刚送进去，还没出门，索尼就把我叫住了，说这个游戏的版本号填错了，这个就不用再测了，直接回去重新弄！”

袁老师：当时发生这个事情以后，整个团队都处在一个惴惴不安的状态，因为传出来要有人担责，这里面压力最大的就是我们的 Data Manager。其实我知道，因为同时开发两个项目，他已经非常尽力了，当时天天陪着团队熬通宵，都已经熬出了熊猫眼。团队可以轮流加班，但他必须一直跟着做版本，我甚至已经做好了自己承担所有责任的准备。所以我当时就跟他说这个完全理解，赶紧再压一个正确版本号的盘就好了。好在后面这个版本一次性通过了，大家悬着的心才放下。虽然《幽灵行动》的开发过程是一波三折，但是这个经历也是我们这条研发线路走向成熟的开始。

中国原创与心流理论

《彩虹六号 3》PS2 版
袁老师收藏

行己：为什么《幽灵行动》代表了这条研发线路走向成熟？

袁老师：因为在《幽灵行动》之后，我们又于 2003 年开发了《彩虹 6 号》三代（PS2 版），整个移植过程已经非常顺利，这说明团队在 3A 游戏的开发模式上已经基本跑通了。这个游戏是基于 XBOX 版移植的，但是由于 PS2 的内存太小了，我们当时的主要工作就是将游戏场景进行分割和重新设计来适应 PS2 的内存限制。这个项目开发了有一年左右，如果回看过往经历，我们从懵懂走向成熟已经经过了 6 年（1998 至 2004）。在《幽灵行动》之后，团队已经不再需要每天去为各种技术问题救火了，大家开始把更多精力用到了内容创作上。所以我后来经常会在交流中提到，《细胞分裂》、《孤岛惊魂 3》这些 3A 内容制作的背后是需要经过好几个项目才能沉淀出来的。

行己：所以当时团队已经开始涉足游戏内容原创方面的工作了么？

袁老师：已经出现一些苗头了，那个时期上海育碧推出了《细胞分裂：明日潘多拉》，我们在《幽灵行动 2》的 PS2 版上也制作了很多原创内容。

行己：《幽灵行动 2》是在什么契机下开始原创内容的？

袁老师：2004 年初我们就接到开发《幽灵行动 2》PS2 版本的需求，1 月份我就去蒙特利尔看了该作的 XBOX 版开发情况。当时这个游戏的 XBOX 版还处于初期阶段，游戏刚做了一张地图。但是总部要求 PS2 版本需要在同年内发售。于是我就建议总部能够让上海育碧同步开发单独的 PS2 版本，这个建议最后被总部采纳了。我记得主程徐小悦用了半个月的时间在 PS2 上搞出了一个很大的场景 DEMO，画面效果很不错，我拿到总部，老板们很满意。我们还招聘了一位美国作家写了故事大纲。2004 年 4 月 1 日我们的项目启动会上我告诉大家这个项目只有 6 个月的时间，听到这个消息以后团队成员不仅没有紧张，反而都非常兴奋准备大干一场，因为大家终于有机会制作自己的 3A 游戏了。

笔者按：如果没有玩过 PS2 版《幽灵行动 2》的朋友可以再去体验一下，因为 PS2 版和 XBOX 版其实是两个独立的游戏。

行己：这个项目是上海育碧完全自主开发的吗？

袁老师：是的，里面所有的场景、玩法、剧情对白，包括所有的音频、音乐都是上海团队独立制作的。不过在开发进行到一个很关键的时候，《细胞分裂：明日潘多拉》从我们组借走了一些骨干人员，因为那个项目当时是上海育碧最重要的项目，所以《明日潘多拉》应该是上海育碧的另一款集大成之作（笑）。另外给大家透露一个 PS2 版的专属彩蛋，《幽灵行动 2》是可以将重力降到 1/10 的，这样击中敌人后，敌人会飞得很远。其实这个设计最早是一个游戏 BUG，我们觉得非常有意思就给保留下来了。具体的解锁方法我有点记不清楚了。

《幽灵行动 2》PS2 版
袁老师收藏

行己：《幽灵行动 2》的制作过程中有什么难忘的事情么？

袁老师：有两件事情非常难忘。一件事是场景设计，另一个是我们的音乐制作。首先是场景设计的故事。当时我们有一个场景设计需求，要体现大战开始前的宁静。我们把这个需求分给了一名外籍设计师，他当时用一座水边的古堡和零星的芦苇丛作为点缀完美的诠释出了这种暴风雨前的宁静感。后来我问他是如何想到的，他告诉我这是他小时候生活过的地方。那个瞬间，我切身感受到了艺术源于生活的意思。有些东西如果我们没见过，真的是再怎么想也想不到的。另外一件事和我们的音乐制作有关。我记得在游戏中有一场战斗是发生在加油站里的，当玩家进入了敌人的埋伏圈，激烈的战斗立刻打响。为了体现战争的残酷性，我们的音乐制作老师特意在加油站上加了一个旧式喇叭，选了一首极度反差，曲调悠扬的朝鲜歌曲作为背景音乐，当画面，声音，玩法融合到一起时，当时所有人都觉得这是个令人起鸡皮疙瘩的场面。但是游戏送到总部以后，法律部门提出这个曲子没有版权不能使用。于是我们就只好将这个音乐去掉了，等封版（制作游戏最终版本）那一天，音乐老师突然找到我，给了我一首曲子，他说这是他和父亲用了一晚上时间创作出来，亲自演奏并录音的，看看能不能加到游戏里。我当时非常感动，就开了一个特例，把这首曲子加进去了。虽然效果可能不如原先那首朝鲜歌曲好，但是那个场景的设计意图依然完整展现出来了。这份热情我到现在还记得。我觉得这件事反映出这个团队当年对这个游戏的热爱有多么强烈，也证明了当团队每个人都把自己的能力充分发挥出来时，结果会多么超出预期。我们那时候真的希望把每一个细节都做到最好，如果项目研发周期不是只有 6 个月就更好了（笑）。

行己：经过这个项目以后您有什么值得分享的经验吗？

袁老师：在《幽灵行动 2》之后我们其实开始了电影化设计的游戏创作过程，这个过程提出的概念其实是对后来游戏设计有一定参考意义的。我记得在做《幽灵行动 2》的时候，总部提出来游戏设计要像好莱坞拍电影一样，能够把握观众的心理体验，做到全程无尿点。为此他们提出了一套可量化的设计理论。这种设计理念其实在 PS1 时期就已经有了雏形，到 PS2 时代的时候被正式命名为“理性游戏设计”。这种方法要求在制作大量内容前，先规划好完整的游戏体验，给整个游戏体验设定好最初的框架。每一个基础游戏性元素，每一段游戏过程，也包括每一段剧情推进，每一个成长解锁，多个要素呼应组合等等，都会在相对抽象的层面被评估对玩家的价值，难度，正反馈还是负反馈等等。在这个阶段设计团队会反复讨论验证规划是否合理有趣，当这个框架确定后，才真正开始内容制作，而这也是团队成员完全释放创意的时刻。比如前面提到的幽灵行动 2 的关卡设计，在黄昏湖边古堡的设计出现之前，我们对这个关卡宏观上的定位是给玩家一个相对舒缓的游戏体验，以迎接下一关更具挑战的战斗，如何表现这个体验，就看大家的创作功力了。这种方法后来在国内游戏界也广泛使用，成了游戏制作入门的基础，在腾讯它叫心流。

法国总统来访

行己：2004 年上海育碧出了好几个游戏吧？

袁老师：对，《幽灵行动 2》、《彩虹 6 号》三代和《细胞分裂：明日潘多拉》都是这一年出的。这一年算是我们的高光之年了，因为 2004 年底法国总统希拉克还在访华期间参观了上海育碧。回想起来，这里边很多人现在都已经是各个行业的风云人物了（笑）。那个时代是上海育碧信心最强的时期。

与希拉克合影
袁老师提供

《细胞分裂 4》与国际化

《细胞分裂 4：双面间谍》XBOX360 版
袁老师收藏

行己：从《细胞分裂：明日潘多拉》开始，育碧是否就准备把这个系列做成“年货”了？

袁老师：我们自己内部没有年货的概念，但是育碧当时希望一个 IP 起来以后，可以通过单数的 1、3、5 代去搞突破，双数的 2、4、6 代来延续 IP 热度。这样既可以维持 IP 热度，也能给 IP 更多的创新时间，在这个思路下制作出来的代表作就是《细胞分裂 3：混沌理论》。不过我们当时制作的是《细胞分裂 4：双面间谍》。

行己：为什么没有参与《细胞分裂 3》的开发呢？

袁老师：因为当时上海育碧的技术实力已经被总部认可，所以我们需要承担下一代主机游戏的开发任务，也就是 PS3、XBOX360 和 PC 平台的游戏开发。《细胞分裂 3》还是在 PS2 和 XBOX 上的作品，因此我们并没有参与。另外，从开发时间上来看，其实 3 代和 4 代在很长一段时间里是并行开发的，但设计目标完全不同。

行己：《细胞分裂 4》的设计思路与前作有什么不同么？

袁老师：因为《细胞分裂 4》是我们做的第一个次世代主机项目，所以当时对于如何发挥好主机性能我们做了很长时间的技术预研，当年实现了好几项 XBOX360 上的技术突破，比如超大量粒子系统，全局光照漫反射等等。4 代的执行制作人也正是 2 代的执行制作人，是从法国派驻上海的，基于这些技术突破带来的画面提升，她提出了 4 代中“在白天玩潜入”的概念。因为白天既能展示出新主机在画面性能上的优势，也能和过往系列形成内容差异。这也就是为何《细胞分裂 4》里会有大量的白天场景。不过更重要的是《双面间谍》是该系列第一个需要进行道德选择的多结局作品。在这一作里，玩家作为 NSA 派到恐怖组织里的卧底必须在任务中进行不同选择以维持两边组织的信任。为了还原这种双面间谍的紧张感和剧情的复杂性，我们在作品中加入了大量过场动画。随着工作量的飙升，团队也快速扩张到了 200 人左右这在管理上带来了更大的挑战，加之又是首次在次世代主机上开发游戏，还采用了全新的剧情玩法设计，在过程中还是走了不少弯路。不过令人欣慰的是这个游戏最终在 IGN 得到了 9 分，GameSpot 也有 8.5 分。这里还有一个插曲，我们在 E3 展上展示《双重间谍》的时候小岛秀夫还来体验了一把，当时大家都很激动。这个场景还被去采访的多边形老师看到了，后来促成了一次上海育碧的专访。

上海育碧专访
（游戏机实用技术 2006.12）

行己：那您离开《双面间谍》项目后还继续制作游戏么？

袁老师：后来我在育碧做了 4 年人事管理工作，参与育碧全球工作室职业发展框架的升级，然后返回研发线，参与了《孤岛惊魂 3》。

自然与创新

《孤岛惊魂 3》PS3 版
袁老师收藏

行己：《孤岛惊魂 3》也是上海育碧制作的么？

袁老师：《孤岛惊魂 3》里的一部分内容是由上海育碧制作的。这个项目最早是蒙特利尔制作的，记得也经过了很长时间的预研，但是最终在原型（Prototype）阶段被总部否决了，许多核心管理人员也都离职了。为此育碧请 Dan Hey 接手了这个项目，另外还请 Craig Hubbard 作为设计顾问。Dan Hey 加入育碧前是《F.E.A.R.3》(极度恐慌 3)的制作人，他的到来对《孤岛惊魂 3》的设计起到了重要作用。Dan Hey 来到上海了解这边的情况以后，决定让我们和蒙特利尔一起合作开发这个项目。如果玩过《孤岛惊魂 3》的话，里面会有一段剧情是寻找一把中国古代匕首，这段内容就是由上海育碧完成的。我记得当时我们为了丰富这段内容不光引入了明朝的地下古墓，设计了整个历史背景，还引入了二战时期日本人遗留的一个军事基地，来增加整体故事的层次感。

行己：在内容创新方面我们有参与吗？

袁老师：《孤岛惊魂 3》上的动物生态是上海设计并制作的，这个系统在 3 代出现，成了系列的标志性内容。如果你留意的话你会发现这个游戏里的野生动物行为非常丰富，它们有时会攻击人类，有时会互相追捕。这些都不是预先设定好的内容，而是基于一个完整的生态链和不同的动物 AI 自发涌现的。这种设计后来被玩家衍生出很多有趣的玩法，比如把一个关着老虎的笼子打开，让老虎去攻击敌人。不过这里也有一些遗憾，就是水中的生物，比如鲨鱼之类的大型食肉动物，但当年我们还很难在三维空间里实现足够真实的行动轨迹，因此最终放弃了水下攻击型生物的生态制作。

笔者按：《孤岛惊魂 3》最广为人知的“动物袭击据点”“生态链干扰战斗”等系统，并非完全来自蒙特利尔，而是由上海育碧负责野生动物 AI 设计与实现，是中国团队参与全球 AAA 核心玩法设计的重要案例。

袁老师：其实这个游戏初期还有一个特别厉害的系统，但是最终因性能问题被放弃了。这个系统就是动态水循环系统。最早我们设计这个岛屿的水流时，是有一个从源头流入大海的完整过程的。而且水体本身也有完整的物理特性，例如玩家可以把油桶弄到，里面的汽油会根据地形流向低洼的地带；炸开水坝，涌下的洪水会和场景中的物体发生真实的物理互动；游戏里的河水会根据岛屿上的水量有上涨和下落。如果截断河流，河水也会溢到岸边。我们还根据这个系统设计了很多玩法。但是最终我们发现受到机能限制，我们很难把水面与地面交汇处的的效果表现得很自然，这就使得水面与地面衔接的地方会非常突兀，所以这个系统最终被放弃了。去年的死亡搁浅 2 除了白金，我还在水边蹲了几个小时，不得不说小岛组的处理是个非常棒的设计（笑）。

行己：当时咱们是怎么想到动物生态和动态水循环系统这些创新点的呢？

袁老师：这就是对于有创新需求的产品，我们会使用所谓“自上而下的设计思路”。首先根据产品的定位和目标，我们会花比较多的时间去确定希望带给玩家的核心体验，最终会浓缩成几句简短的话或关键词，给产品划下了清晰的范围。再基于这些核心体验去头脑风暴，找到最能够烘托体验的表现方式。以此不断地深挖下去，确保最终所有内容，都是服务于一个统一的，逻辑合理的目标。例如：《孤岛惊魂 3》的顶层体验目标就是荒岛求生，在这个基础上我们将体验关键词定义为，异域自然风情、危险与未知。在这个基础上我们会开展头脑风暴，思考哪些内容和设计可以用来展现这些关键词。最后我们确定了 4 个设计目标，并推导出了所对应的具体设计。虽然在最终产品中因为各种原因放弃了大量内容，但最终展示出来的内容依然很好的服务了核心体验的目标。

《孤岛惊魂 3》的创意逻辑

行己：这种合作开发的方式是否会有很高的沟通成本？

袁老师：这个游戏实际上是蒙特利尔、上海和瑞典三方一起开发的，因为我们的生态系统涉及到很多游戏引擎的底层改动，因此开会是非常频繁的，那时候每周都有两次电话会议。而且我们还和蒙特利尔有 12 小时的时差，就只能是找一个两边都方便的时间，最后定的是每周二和周四双方轮流早八点，对方晚八点开会。不过真正麻烦的是快到封板的时候很多同学还要去加拿大实地工作，我作为制作人频繁往来两地，记得最频繁的一个月我跑了三趟蒙特利尔，当时已经完全没有时差这个概念了，白天黑夜完全就乱了都不知道当年是怎么挺下来的。好在这个游戏上市后反响还不错，这个 IP 也被复活了。

笔者按：《孤岛惊魂 3》（Far Cry3）最终销量超过 2000 万，成为奠定该系列历史地位的核心作品。

20 年后回看游戏创新

行己：经过这么多年的经验积累，您认为单机游戏开发里最重要的是什么？

袁老师：我认为最重要的还是做游戏的初心，做一个好玩的游戏，讲一个好故事。一个好的创意是游戏成功的基础。现在游戏产业在美术制作和技术实现上都已经非常成熟了，各种美术风格和技术效果都能够实现。因此真正能够让游戏形成竞争力的是与众不同的创意。对于电影化叙事的游戏来说，讲故事的能力是关键，而一个好故事的基础是主创的深厚沉淀和与众不同的视角。这里不得不多说一点：提出一个好创意，和把好创意做成一个好游戏又完全是两回事，今天就不展开了吧。

行己：如何做到与众不同呢？

袁老师：我认为首先是创作者要有丰富的阅历，只有看过，经历过，思考过才有机会想到。就好像我们在制作《幽灵行动 2》时的那位关卡设计师，他把儿时的场景搬到了游戏里。如果他没有这段儿时经历，只是从网上查询资料的话恐怕很难拥有那种身临其境的感觉，也不可能把那种感觉塑造到那个游戏场景中。其次我认为还需要有以小见大的逻辑思维能力，好比《33 号远征队》或其他一些游戏的世界观设定，他们在一种成熟的世界观上做了微小调整，但却可以根据这些细节上的变化，基于逻辑推理，形成一套与其他游戏截然不同的世界观，从而讲述出一个差异盎然却感人至深的故事。

行己：对于现在的游戏开发者您有什么建议呢？

袁老师：现在新一代的开发者要比我们的经历更加丰富，更容易产生好的创意和想法。不过对于游戏设计来说，如果能本着源于生活高于生活的方式来创作可能会事半功倍。随着游戏开发门槛的大幅降低，AI agent 在游戏行业的广泛应用，未来游戏同质化会越来越严重，而产生这种同质化的一个重要原因可能是大家基于过往的游戏经历去制作游戏，而真正能形成差异化竞争力的游戏创意往往不是来自其他游戏，而是来自现实生活，所以希望大家能多体验不同的新鲜事物，把游戏制作当作一种表达方式，用游戏去展现生活中的特色和乐趣也是游戏创新的一种方法。

行己：好的，谢谢您。

结语

上海育碧从做技术移植到主导项目的过程既是一个向全世界展示中国游戏开发实力的过程，也是一个不断拼搏证明自己的过程。无论是工期上的压力还是设计上的分歧，每一次都需要有人能顶住压力，有人能解决问题，团队拥有超常的凝聚力。而将这个中国团队凝聚在一起的也许就是他们的执着、热情和工匠精神。最终，这个团队一次次的用实力赢得了市场，用优异的市场表现赢得了总公司的信任，用连续的成功赢得了项目的主导权。随着时代的发展和公司的变化，这些当年的开发者或已创业，或成为了中国游戏公司的“顶梁柱”。如今，这些曾经在育碧开发游戏时的梦想与热情，正在用来书写属于中国人自己的游戏大作。

文中部分游戏历史价值

《幽灵行动》PS2 版

开发周期：1 年
上市时间：2002 年 12 月

历史意义：

1、现代战术射击游戏的代表作之一，对《武装突袭》《Ready or Not》《战术小队》等真实战术射击路线产生间接影响；
2、PC 硬核战术 FPS 向主机迁移的早期尝试之一；
3、体现了中国团队在 3A 游戏设计上的早期尝试。


《幽灵行动 2》PS2 版

开发周期：10 个月
上市时间：2004 年 11 月

历史意义：

1、中国团队主导的唯一一部《幽灵行动》作品；
2、战术射击向主机大众化转型的重要案例。

——完——

——《次世代中国造，独家专访上海育碧》多边形 （游戏机实用技术 2006.12）

发行日期： 2026/11/02（ 中文支持 ）

Feed The Forest
关键字： 增量
发行日期： 2026/11/02（ 中文支持 ）
运用蜗牛之力，将沙漠变成郁郁葱葱的森林，然后在这款主动增量游戏中疯狂追求利润最大化。优化植物布局，自动化生产各类资源。雇佣爪牙，解锁非道德植物，变得富可敌神吧。记住：鲜血也是一种汁液。
The Rusted
关键字： 2D 平台、动作冒险、解谜
发行日期： 2026/11/02（ 中文支持 ）
世界如今属于机器。陪伴一只忠诚的机器狗，穿越阴森的末日世界，踏上寻找失散人类家人的旅程。《THE RUSTED》是一款手绘风格的 2D 动作解谜平台游戏。
Sabado
关键字： 心理恐怖、步行模拟
发行日期： 2026/11/02（ 中文支持 ）
与最要好的同学重逢，但你永远无法真正从过去中毕业……和一位名叫切萨的开朗朋友一起，在充满怀旧气息、不断变幻的高中回忆迷宫中徜徉。然而，出口正在消失，走廊正在扭曲，而一位沉默的观察者正密切关注着你的每一步。
手动取款机（Manual Teller Machine）
关键字： 生活模拟、时间管理
发行日期： 2026/11/02（ 中文支持 ）
在这款上班模拟器中，你将扮演一名躲在 ATM 背后的员工，负责处理主管交办下来的大小事。透过完成各种任务、解锁奖励，甚至是争取加薪！同时还要管理好每一天的时间，兼顾食材与身材，也别忘了用你的薪水好好犒赏自己。

关键字： 商店管理、轻度 Rogue
发行日期： 2026/11/02（ 中文支持 ）
节奏飞快的肉鸽经营游戏！限时 30 天内赚到 100 万，扩建桌椅，升级菜谱，雇佣培训店员，打造属于你的赚钱机器！每局随机获得厨师、菜谱与经营道具，自由搭配不同流派，节日庆典限时开启，寻找让收益暴涨的隐藏组合，不断解锁更强力的赚钱道具，挑战多种经营路线，解锁属于你的隐藏结局。每 10 天迎来一次大股东考核，能否撑到第 30 天，完成 100 万元业绩？
Dance of Drauganna
关键字： VR、节奏、奇幻
发行日期： 2026/11/02（暂无中文）
《Dance of Drauganna》是一款叙事 VR 节奏舞蹈游戏，玩家将通过舞蹈穿越各种生命形态，从昆虫到机器人，再到外星生物。该作融合了动作捕捉技术、原创电子音乐和互动式叙事，探索了万物之间的相互联系。
我亲爱的.exe（MyDear.exe）
关键字： 短篇、爱情、放松
发行日期： 2026/11/02（ 中文支持 ）
在《我亲爱的.exe》里，和艾莉与卢西安一起庆祝一段爱情。这是一个短小温馨的游戏，故事藏在一台老式电脑的文件夹里。你将扮演艾莉，打开丈夫卢西安在两人相伴大半生后为她准备的游戏。幽默、回忆和爱，都装在这段约两小时的小小旅程中。
Blobby and the Milkshake
关键字： 2D 平台、欢乐、动作冒险
发行日期： 2026/11/02（暂无中文）
一只章鱼偷走了你的奶昔。为什么？谁知道呢！在这款滑稽有趣、开放式的 2D 平台游戏中，骑着机器人螃蟹，驾驶消防栓飞行，在浴缸里滑行，与贪婪的海盗蛤蜊展开战斗。探索数十个关卡，选择不同的路线，不惜一切代价夺回你的饮料。
Figure Me Out
关键字： 社交聚会游戏、欢乐、潜行
发行日期： 2026/11/03（ 中文支持 ）
一款多人第一人称射击游戏，玩家需通过输入对手额头上的数字来消灭对手。在对手读出你的数字之前先读出他们的数字，利用战术道具扰乱战局，并在最多 20 名玩家参与的对战中与好友或陌生人一决高下。
日进斗金（PlinkIdle）
关键字： 增量、街机
发行日期： 2026/11/03（ 中文支持 ）
开局一颗小球，点燃无限混乱与惊喜！看它们在钉板间弹跳、分裂，看金币从涓涓细流变成财富瀑布。升级钉子和奖池，解锁主题关卡与独特音效，掉落效率与奖励倍率节节攀升！华丽光效清脆音效带来视听盛宴，每一次下落都让人欲罢不能！
Mayday: The Survival Island
关键字： 开放世界生存制作、沙盒
发行日期： 2026/11/03（ 中文支持 ）
坠机后，你独自醒来。通过狩猎、耕种与制作生存，并探索充满秘密的群岛。建造基地、揭开真相、逃离此地——如果你能做到。
GRAVHOUNDS
关键字： 在线合作、基地建设、动作类 Rogue
发行日期： 2026/11/03（暂无中文）EA
《GRAVHOUNDS》是一款可供 1-4 名玩家合作游玩的动作建造游戏。你们将共同降落至敌对星球，应对遵循真实物理法则的混乱场面，建造并守护基地，并要在沦为外星人的食物之前，尽可能地带着所有物品撤离！坚守的时间越久，危险就越大……但奖励也越丰厚。
IRON SOL
关键字： 平台游戏、低容错
发行日期： 2026/11/03（暂无中文）
你无需解锁任何能力——你只是将揭开关于自己一直以来所具备的能力的真相。探索一片废墟世界，克服独特的平台跳跃挑战，收集同族留下的残骸，并发现自己的真实身份。
BOOST VECTOR EX
关键字： 竞速、跑酷、3D 平台
发行日期： 2026/11/03（暂无中文）
跑得比任何人都快！掌控“矢量大师”，在极限史诗级赛道上驰骋。体验真正的跑酷竞速。磨练你的风格，凭借强劲、迅捷的操控成为最强者。在矢量世界杯中夺得冠军。你够快吗？
音飙（Beat For Speed）
关键字： 基于音乐的程序生成、节奏、摩托车
发行日期： 2026/11/03（ 中文支持 ）
将任何歌曲变成可玩的节奏骑行之旅！导入你喜欢的音乐，或通过实时音频模式跟随电脑播放的音乐游玩。我们基于数千个手工制作关卡的创作经验打造了专属节奏系统，将你最爱的音乐变成动态赛道。探索来自独立音乐人的官方曲目，挑战排行榜，上手游戏内置的关卡编辑器和 Steam 创意工坊。你可以创作自己独一无二的关卡，也可以探索创意工坊中源源不断的来自全球玩家的丰富作品。
弗莱明庄园命案（Death at Fleming Manor）
关键字： 悬疑、推理、调查
发行日期： 2026/11/03（ 中文支持 ）
“你的工作是填写死亡证明。” 调查 1959 年英国庄园中发生的神秘死亡事件。探索阴森的现场，分析证据，并填写死亡证明和急救报告。这是一款法医推理游戏，画面风格灵感来自 20 世纪 60 年代的欧洲侦探漫画。
Shin'ai Rewritten
关键字： 农场模拟、角色扮演
发行日期： 2026/11/03（暂无中文）
在这款温馨的生活模拟 RPG 中，前往日本乡间与祖父重聚，为祖母的花园注入新活力，并结识当地居民。
Ribbit Riot!
关键字： 短篇、破坏、增量、上帝模拟
发行日期： 2026/11/03（暂无中文）
《Ribbit Riot!》是一款单键混乱游戏，你将释放一群傻乎乎的青蛙来摧毁一座小城。点击青蛙按钮，叠加各种荒诞的升级道具，然后看着一切彻底失控。
Terminidle
关键字： 增量、黑客
发行日期： 2026/11/03（暂无中文）
《Terminidle》是一款增量黑客游戏，玩家需从一个简陋的终端中挖掘数据。培育僵尸网络、执行黑客合约，并不断升级你的设备，直到它能启动完整的桌面操作系统，甚至可能实现更多功能！然后清除所有数据以获得永久能量，从而更快地重新攀升！
How Empires Work
关键字： 增量、策略、自动化
发行日期： 2026/11/03（ 中文支持 ）
这是一款增量式大战略游戏，由你亲手来打造帝国机器。征税、通商、征服、开化——无论本国臣民还是异邦人，总之一视同仁。让这些事务实现自动化，形成一套能在数百年的历史变迁中自行运转的制度体系。 女皇陛下要看到你的成果。
第二部分
下一部分明日送上！

title: I'm glad that WoW: Forever'll have a slower, lo-fi update schedule, because I'm not playing this thing to be in a rush
author: Harvey Randall
text:
Harvey Randall
(Image credit: Future) I've played about 50+ hours of the World of Warcraft: Forever beta, and wouldn't you know it, I'm going to be playing a lot more when it comes out November 4.
Earlier this week, Kris Zierhut, principal game designer on World of Warcraft: Forever, said that the game would have a release schedule that's a "little more laid back" . Rather than the blisteringly fast eight to 10 week schedule of Season of Discovery, Forever'll aim to release major updates once every four months or so.
This is honestly music to my ears—I've been impressed by retail WoW's blistering pace and its seasonal structure, even if there have been some rocky, bug-filled patches in the past; and it's certainly something I've praised before, especially in contrast to other certain MMOs that have been coming to a standstill.
But I've been playing WoW… well, for a long time, but I've had a consistent sub since Dragonflight, and I've been able to see the arc of Blizzard whipping up its schedule into a proper roadmap . Which did pull the game back from the brink, true, but three expansions in and I'm just sort of exhausted.
There's always some new bar to fill, some new doohickey to collect, some new reputation track to chew on, and it all moves so fast that if I, say, have an off-week to go play another game, I feel pretty lost. While Midnight does major patches at roughly the same release tempo (12.0.0 came out in January, 12.1.0 came out in August) it also has a ton of interim stuff to flood out your schedule every three months, rather than four.
Launch was already crammed with stuff—a raid tier, delves, the new prey system, housing, and so on. Just under three months passed since launch, and wham, suddenly we've got Void Assaults! Ritual Sites! The Omnium Folio! Whatever Abyss Anglers is, I never checked, which is kinda the problem! Just over a month later, and there's a new raid and a new system plugged into Void Assaults (which I'm literally just now finding out about, I completely missed it). Two months later, and it's 12.1.0, which I hadn't even sat down to properly play before Labyrinths became a thing.
The idea of smaller, chiller patches in an overall slower-paced game (here's fellow PCG writer Lincoln Carpenter's treatise on the virtues of hitting a scorpion with a club for 38 seconds ) sounds like a nice, soothing bath after an overstimulating day at the circus.
I do feel that prickling sense of overstimulation fear return when Zierhut talks about the interim stuff, however:
"And then one nuance on that is: We do plan on making content that unlocks in between … you want to stagger out some content across those four months. It's not just patch day comes [around], here's a content fire hose, and now we're silent for four months. A lot of that is, hey, there's a time event calendar that gradually unlocks things and opens them up over those four months to give things a little bit more life instead of that all at once effect."
Still, given Forever's meant to be a horizontally-progressing game that doesn't have expansions ( we'll need to see how that pans out ), I might find these little tasks a lot more soothing than the looming feeling I have with WoW, where at any point it might suddenly become too late to get stuck into a season.
Ideally, these mid-patch trickles will be optional tasks I can get around to basically whenever, rather than something I feel pressured to get done just so I can stay up-to-date for whatever flashy system's trundling down the pipeline next. Hit me with that lo-fi update cadence, I'm ready for it.

title: It's not just Steam: New game pages created per day on Itch.io have doubled in the last two months, with AI slop the likely culprit
author: Rick Lane
text:
It seems it isn't just Steam that's being flooded with AI slop. Indie games storefront itch.io has reported that the number of new game pages being created per day on the site has doubled in the past two months, and just like Valve's much bigger distribution service, the finger is being pointed at AI.
Over on Bluesky, itch.io shared an image of a bar chart labelled "game events". The chart shows that, between August 3 and October 30, the number of new game pages being created per day has risen from around 3,000 to regularly surpassing 6,000. It's a ratio that more or less matches the increase in Steam demos showcased at the most recent Next Fest , which rose from around 4,000 to over 8,000.
While Itch doesn't explicitly point the finger at AI as the cause, it heavily infers it. When Bluesky user Tommy's Homemade Games asked "Do you know why?" Itch responded "take a guess" followed by emojis of a crying face and a robot. Another Bluesky account, BardZaku, asked "is it AI dreck?" to which the account replied with an emoji of a face with bags under its eyes.
The rapid uptick in Itch pages also coincides with the launch of Claude Opus 5, which arrived on July 24. The latest iteration of Anthropic's LLM—which is now at version 5.5—has proved particularly adept at reverse engineering code. This has had a bunch of knock-on effects in various areas of game development, ranging from much faster decompilations of old games, to Steam being flooded with AI slop, and developers cancelling public demos out of concerns their games will be cloned.
Anthropic has since updated Claude to reign in its ability to directly copy games, but it's currently hard to tell whether it has stemmed the broader flow of AI generated games. Indeed, it's worth pointing out that AI Generated games now comprise a good portion of the pages listed on Itch. Out of 1,769,316 listed on Itch at the time of writing, 131,929 are tagged as AI Generated, approximately 7.5% of the total. That's a lot, considering how long AI coding tools have been around.
But to play devil's advocate, Itch is a storefront that allows AI games, and if people are downloading and enjoying these games, then adding them to the store is fair enough, right? Well , Itch also points out that, although the number of games appearing on Itch per day has doubled, "the number of downloads and purchases has *not* doubled". This suggests these AI games are clogging up the site for nobody's benefit, not even the people 'making' them.
The question, then, is what's to be done about all this? The replies to Itch's initial post are filled with calls to ban AI generated games from the store. But as pointed out by AI researcher Mike Cook, simply banning these games is unlikely to solve the problem.
"I think that would be a good move. But it won't change this graph, unfortunately," Cook wrote on Bluesky. "You need a team of people to enforce it, or a very dicey public reporting system. Even then, it's a lot harder to detect than people think." Valve has also cast doubt on the efficacy of a ban on AI coding tools for games released on Steam, though its opinion is heavily influenced by the company's laissez-faire approach to operating its storefront.
Another possibility is to simply let this trend play out. There is a viral element to the ongoing surge in AI generated games, as people post their vibe-coded works online for attention and social media clout. But Itch's statement suggests that people aren't properly engaging with most of the games being uploaded.
Hence, it's possible that the people behind these games may eventually lose interest, moving on to whatever attention-grabbing scheme big tech facilitates next. The risk, of course, is that the audience also loses interest in what these storefronts offer before that happens. After all, nobody wants to wade through a tsunami of slop to get to the games they want to play.

title: Chronicles: Medieval developer faces imminent closure after losing funding: 'What makes it hurt is how close we are. Early access is in reach'
author: Rick Lane
text:
Chronicles: Medieval is an impressive looking open-world sandbox where players explore a dynamic Medieval world and fight in massive, authentic battles. It's been in development for more than four years and is due to launch into Steam early access early in 2027.
However, there is a very real chance this will no longer happen, as developer Raw Power Games suddenly faces closure after funding for its game was pulled.
On Friday, Raw Power Games posted a statement to Steam and on social media channels (via IGN ), explaining how the studio has suddenly found itself in dire straits. "Due to circumstances outside our control, the necessary funding for Raw Power Games is no longer in place," the studio wrote. "Without it, we can't keep building Chronicles: Medieval, and right now the studio is at real risk of closing."
This appears to be a sudden development. Through October, the studio had been posting regular development updates, including an incredibly detailed deep dive on Medieval coats of arms and how they would appear in the game. None of it suggested a studio that's in trouble, so it seems this has caught Raw Power off guard.
By the sounds of it, Chronicles: Medieval isn't all that far away from being done, either. Or at least ready for its planned alpha launch: "What makes it hurt is how close we are. Early access is within reach," Raw Power Games writes in its statement. "The world we've been building for years is finally starting to feel alive, and we have so much we've been thrilled to show you."
Chronicles: Medieval first appeared on our radar last year , not without some controversy. At the time, Raw Power Games was super excited about using generative AI for its games. Not only was the studio using Midjourney to generate (terrible) concept art, but company COO Jakob Rasmussen told Danish newspaper Ingeniøren that genAI was "at the core of our vision", adding that "When the technology is ready—and perhaps a little sooner—we'll be willing to stick our necks out and put it into the game."
Yet the company quickly changed its tune on this point, with CTO Caspar Strandbygaard telling PC Gamer that Chronicles: Medieval was "100% handcrafted with no use of generative AI." Strandbygaard admitted that Raw Power was still "curious" about the technology, but regarding Chronicles specifically, he stressed that "every asset in the game is built by our extremely talented team of passionate developers. It is not generated by AI."
While the situation seems grim for Raw Power, the studio says that it is "not going down without a fight" and has urged fans of the game to "keep Chronicles: Medieval on your wishlist and keep talking about it." How much road Raw Power has remaining before it's forced to close isn't clear. But since the game is allegedly close to being in a releasable state, it may be able to secure new funding relatively soon.

title: 'An absolute behemoth': Wildly ambitious FPS Selaco is getting a massive update that doubles its size and adds 'a heavy machinegun that fires literal explosions'
author: Rick Lane
text:
If you're a fan of first-person shooters and haven't played Selaco , you should. Built in the Doom engine and inspired by FEAR , Half-Life and System Shock , Selaco is a rollicking, dizzyingly ambitious sci-fi FPS where you battle a mercenary incursion of a vast, city-sized space station that's home to the last of humanity.
Launched into Steam early access in 2024, Selaco's first chapter alone is as long as some entire '90s shooters. Now, developer Altered Orbit Studios is preparing to release an update that will not only double the length of the game, but also introduce a wide array of new features and rework much of its existing design.
Described by Altered Orbit as "an absolute behemoth", Selaco: The Machines of War introduces the second of a planned three chapters to the FPS. Chapter two comprises 19 new campaign maps, which apparently amounts to "6-8 hours of additional content". Alongside further story elements and a voice for the protagonist, the chapter also introduces what sounds like a persistent enemy, in the form of "an unstoppable machine" that is "hunting you down."
Naturally, this second chapter also adds new weapons and enemies, with the former including a minigun and "a heavy machine gun that fires literal explosions". I don't know how that would work, but I'm keen to find out! Alongside your equipped arsenal, players will be able to use new deployable weapons like mini-turrets and sentinel drones, while the update also introduces a "heavy ordnance system" that lets you wield large, disposable weapons scattered across the battlefield, Gears of War -style.
As well as completely new stuff, Altered Orbit says the update will also enhance a lot of existing content. The FEAR inspired enemy AI, for example, has been "rewritten almost entirely from scratch" to facilitate smarter tactics and better decision making. The rewrite also introduces a new "rally" system and NPC area patrolling when not in combat—an addition designed to give players more agency in when and how fighting begins. Oh, and the entire first chapter has been given an overhaul that introduces "improved set pieces" and "new surprises".
And those are just the headline changes. Other improvements mentioned by Altered Orbit include a new lighting system, an overhauled particle system to make combat even more spectacular, improved navigation through Selaco's massive, mazey levels, new voice lines to make enemy communication even more lifelike, better controls, new music, and more. It almost sounds too good to be true, but I've played Chapter 1 and I know Altered Orbit can cook with rocket fuel, so none of this is beyond the studio's capability.
Selaco: The Machines of War arrives on November 13. The scale of the changes means that old saves will no longer be compatible. But if you don't fancy replaying the reworked first episode, you will be able to jump in at the outset of Chapter 2.

Oh, and the entire first chapter has been given an overhaul that introduces "improved set pieces" and "new surprises".

And those are just the headline changes. Other improvements mentioned by Altered Orbit include a new lighting system, an overhauled particle system to make combat even more spectacular, improved navigation through Selaco's massive, mazey levels, new voice lines to make enemy communication even more lifelike, better controls, new music, and more. It almost sounds too good to be true, but I've played Chapter 1 and I know Altered Orbit can cook with rocket fuel, so none of this is beyond the studio's capability.

Selaco: The Machines of War arrives on November 13. The scale of the changes means that old saves will no longer be compatible. But if you don't fancy replaying the reworked first episode, you will be able to jump in at the outset of Chapter 2.

title: Composer and designer Lena Raine explains how Pigstep altered Minecraft's approach to music: 'The prompt I keep hearing is "Oh, Pigstep was such a banger that they want more bangers"'
author: Rick Lane
text:
Disk Cleanup
(Image credit: Future) Welcome to Disk Cleanup , our regular weekend feature delving into the PCs of PC gaming luminaries. Come back every weekend to read a new interview, digging into the important questions, like "How tidy is your desktop?" and "What game will you never uninstall?"
Lena Raine's formative gaming experience was playing Myst on a Mac Quadra 610, exploring Cyan Worlds' enigmatic island in parallel with her father: "We each had our own playthrough, so we were sending each other notes in the little journal that it came with," she says. "I still have the little book that we wrote in."
Raine always aspired to be a composer for video games, but she initially joined the industry as a games tester for Nintendo America, working several other testing jobs before being hired by ArenaNet as a game designer. While working on Guild Wars 2 , Raine designed a bell-choir minigame for the MMO's Winter's Day Christmas update, including writing the music for it. "It was a bizarre first-step into game music," she says. "But that eventually led to at last some visibility for the other music I was writing."
After leaving ArenaNet, Raine wrote the soundtrack for 2018's Celeste , and spent several years composing music for Minecraft , including several of its most popular 'Disc' tracks like Pigstep , Creator , and Otherside . Raine is currently writing music for the early access volleyball RPG Beastieball , while also returning to game design with her own project ANOTHEREAL , an RPG with schmup-style combat. "I have been working on [it] basically since the pandemic," she says. "I'm trying to aim to have something released within the decade."
Raine took a break from her various projects to show me around the digital concert hall of her steam library. We discussed Deadlock , sorted her schmup collection, and took a trip down MMO memory lane.
What game are you currently playing?
(Image credit: Valve) The current game that I'm playing is Deadlock. I've been playing it for a while now, basically since it was pretty early in that beta, alpha, whatever phase. I play with my wife and some other friends that we've got.
I've been having a lot of fun with it. I've never been a MOBA person and I've never been a competitive shooter person either. Usually, I get tremendously frustrated with online competitive shooters because I'm not very good. I'm not great at those sorts of games.
But I love the style and the world that Valve has made for Deadlock. I love spooky occult stuff. I just love that entire vibe. A lot of my personal online characters are like demon girl aesthetics, and so I'm just like "This is a game for me".
I've been really committed to learning at least one character, so I've been focusing on Ivy, which is the gargoyle. She's awesome. She's from the first set of characters. I initially just laser-focussed on her. I was just like "Oh, she's really cool".
What was the previous game you played, and is it still installed
(Image credit: SFB Games) The Mermaid Mask . I was playing it on the Steam Machine, so technically it's still installed. But it's a single-player, linear story game, so I will probably uninstall it at some point to save space.
It's still installed because I finished it yesterday, or two days ago. But I really loved that game. I played the previous game— Tangle Tower —in the Detective Grimoire series, and they just have such a playful way of designing characters and presenting them. The voice acting is really good. The mysteries are fun and interesting to figure out as you're playing through it. It's a detective point-and-click adventure, gathering clues and talking to all the suspects.
There's just [a] ridiculous amount of items in the game that you can ask everyone about. And it's all just voice dialogue about all of them. I'm just such a completionist about it. I just sit in front of the TV and I've been listening to the characters talk about 30 different items for an hour.
What is the oldest game (by release date) currently installed on your PC?
(Image credit: Square Enix) The one that I really wanted to talk about is Final Fantasy 11 , which is one of the first PC games that I got fully obsessed with when I was younger, at high school into college basically. It's got uninstalled and reinstalled over the years. But I have it installed. I've checked in on my character, who has been there since the initial release date … I played a little Tarutaru character and mostly was a red mage and monk.
The interesting piece of history with me and Final Fantasy 11 is that I initially imported it from Japan. It has since transferred over to English servers primarily. But when I initially started playing the game, it was not out in the US yet, and you had to import the game. You had to make a Japanese account with a Japanese address. But there were forums set up for people that wanted to import the game.
So I joined these forums, and these were people who also played like Phantasy Star Online on the Dreamcast, so we were all buzzing about this new game Final Fantasy 11. So there were instructions of like "here's translated screenshots of every single setup thing to do."
I had taken one year of Japanese in high school. So I knew enough to navigate a menu. I didn't know how to converse very well in Japanese, but I knew what the characters for like black mage, red mage, warrior, attack, level up, those sorts of things.
[But] the thing about Final Fantasy 11 is it was such a deeply social game, because to level up past a certain point you needed to join a party. You could not solo past a certain point. So people would group in in levelling parties, and unless I was playing with friends, I would be in a group of Japanese players that I was trying to communicate with, and it really depended on the sophistication of the conversation that was going on that I could blend in or out myself as speaking English.
The majority of friendships that I had was with the English-speaking community, and it's funny because a number of those people have gone on to have some pretty illustrious careers. One of the people that I played with was Maximilian Dood, who's a fairly well-to-do YouTuber now. Another friend that I played PSO and Final Fantasy with was Jason Oestreicher who worked for Giant Bomb for a while. So I have these weird industry connections from playing this import Final Fantasy game years ago.
What is the highest number of hours you have in any given game, according to Steam?
(Image credit: FromSoftware) The highest number of hours is Elden Ring at 282 hours. However, not on Steam, I looked this up also, Final Fantasy 14 , I logged into my character and did the playtime conversion, and it's 1,308 hours.
I feel like I've talked a lot about Final Fantasy, [so] to talk a little bit about Elden Ring. I've played pretty much all of the Dark Souls games and mostly attempted to do co-op with them because my wife and I love to play the games together, and we always have a very rough experience when it comes to FromSoft online stuff, because it's very insistent on opening yourself up to adversity when you're playing together with friends.
But with Elden Ring, when that came out, this was right before we moved to Canada … [when] we were in this transit dead space where all our stuff is half-packed and we just need to find the right place. And so we were just calming our brains down by playing Elden Ring together.
That also includes the DLC up until the final boss, because the final boss of the DLC was too steep of a difficulty curve for the build that we were both running. This was also at the time the person that got famous for soloing Melania, they came back and they were Let Me Solo Them instead. And so my wife actually summoned that person, who beat the final boss for her. I was extremely jealous.
What game will you never, ever uninstall?
(Image credit: Cave Interactive) It's a tricky question for me because, with Steam existing as a service, it's very difficult to not uninstall something if you need to save space. But I was looking at what I did have installed and I saw a pattern, which is I basically leave all my favourite schmups installed.
I love going back to games like ZeroRanger , Adventures of Ten and Till , Deathsmiles , Mushihimesama , a number of classic and newer schmups that I love playing, because it's that kind of arcade experience [where] it never gets old. You can keep going back to it, keep improving on it. It's been good research also, because I'm working on a game that has schmup combat in it. But I'm making it because I have this experience with schmups of not being great at them.
A lot of times it has to do with the music too. A really good schmup soundtrack is basically an album.
What's a piece of non-gaming software installed on your PC that you simply couldn't live without?
(Image credit: Bitwig) This one's easy because I'm a composer and I work on the computer, so it's my music software. My DAW of choice right now is Bitwig Studio . It's by ex-developers of Ableton . They split off and made this new DAW called Bitwig that is like if you took a bunch of chains off Ableton in a way where you an rewire everything under the hood.
There's just a really open approach to how it's designed, where you can use basically every version of VST, which is instrument software, that's out there. You can use Clap , which is an open-source plugin format. It can open files from Ableton. It can open files and import the settings and metadata and stuff.
It's the one that has won me over. I've been using Ableton since working on Celeste, because used to use Cakewalk Sonar . The very first piece of music that I wrote for Celeste, I wrote in Cakewalk Sonar, and then I switched to Ableton after that … I literally can't open the first level of Celeste anymore, because it's in software I don't have installed anymore.
The very first [Minecraft update] I worked on was the revitalisation of the Nether, which was the underworld space, and I was pulling from a bunch of survival horror vibes, writing this scary music that was really unsettling, which is funny that that was the first … because the existing tracks that Daniel, C418, did was very calming, soothing.
What most people know my Minecraft music as is the three discs that I wrote, as opposed to the tons of other tracks that I wrote … it's funny because, for [Pigstep] too it was just the developers saying to me, "For discs, you just write whatever you want" because the initial discs were just tunes that C418 wrote that wasn't necessarily related to anything.
One of the throwaway ideas was "What would music the Piglins listen to sound like?" And so I was just like "Dubstep for pigs!" That was the prompt that I made for myself, and I just made a funny little tune and people just love it.
It's created a funny effect. I think at Mojang now, because they've since worked with a couple other composers—I feel like my tenure has expired. I had some fun there, but I want to focus on other projects—but they've worked with other composers since then. But the prompt I keep hearing is 'Oh, Pigstep was such a banger that they want more bangers.' I started something there. It's gonna keep on getting discs that are bangers.
Generally, how tidy is your desktop screen?
Immaculate. I don't really believe in putting anything on my desktop. I have my wallpaper, and it's a cute piece of art, and if I have anything minimised, I look at the art, and I have a folder structure for everything else.

title: Valve's long-lost prototype Portal prequel appears online after nearly 20 years
author: Ted Litchfield
text:
As reported by Kotaku , a near-mythical canceled Valve game called F-Stop has been reconstructed from material contained in separate leaks. Direct access to the build seems a little shaky at the moment, but full playthroughs of the game, like this one by Meme Man? on YouTube , are starting to pop up online.
Most of F-Stop's assets came out in this August's Steam "teraleak," but the final pieces⁠—F-Stop's source code and mapsrc data⁠—were only just acquired by the Valve Cut Content Team Discord, which appears to have gone private amid all the newfound attention over F-Stop. With the Discord currently invite-only, you gotta know a guy (or know a guy who knows a guy) to play it yourself.
The Half-Life Wiki has the skinny on F-Stop's origins in the "Directed Design Experiments." Following the megahit launch of the Orange Box in 2007, Gabe Newell effectively shut Valve down for a three-month game jam that produced five prototypes, F-Stop among them.
It applied Team Fortress 2's cel-shaded art style to a vision of Aperture Science in its prime, all mid-century wood-paneled office optimism. F-Stop's central mechanic was a camera that could capture objects in the world, then place them elsewhere to solve puzzles. The excellent 2023 game Viewfinder would apply a similar concept to a full commercial release.
But while loved internally at Valve, F-Stop's playtests were apparently more tepid. The game was shelved, though elements of its worldbuilding would appear in Portal 2 and Aperture Desk Job. It's fun to recognize some of these early ideas in the F-Stop longplays: From the jump, we get a version of Cave Johnson (sadly sans-J.K. Simmons in prototype) talking to the player, as well as the first instance of Aperture Personality Cores as companions in the puzzling.
Given F-Stop's "road not taken" nature, particularly compared to the megathit Left 4 Dead and Portal 2 that would follow, I don't really mourn the fact that we never got to play its final version. It is, however, extremely cool that the prototype game is now preserved for posterity.

title: GOG wants to bring back physical games, but it's 'a very, very complicated thing'
author: Justin Wagner
text:
I remember when I'd get bored as a kid, I'd marvel at the back covers of my older brother's PC game boxes—stuff like Guild Wars: Factions and the original World of Warcraft box, the inner cover of which showed a dwarf thwacking a yeti with that one epic sword that looked like a lightsaber. Even back then, the long switch to digital was underway, seemingly for good. But what if we could go back to the glory days of big, embossed boxes and girthy manuals?
That's the "dream" of GOG's senior business development and partnerships manager, Marcin Paczynski, as he recently told Gamesradar . Specifically, he wants to see a world where you "would be able to buy physical versions of [games] on GOG … You go to your shelf on GOG, you click on the game that you would like to receive a physical copy of, you order it, and it gets to you. That would be a perfect scenario."
I'm sure most PC gaming diehards would agree that, yes, an option to buy physical games—especially older games in a precarious state with regard to preservation—would be pretty neat. Even if you're the sort to snag DRM-free copies of everything you own, a disc makes a game easier to show off, keep close in the event that your hard drive explodes, or place in the seat across from you at a Michelin star restaurant.
The problem for GOG is that physical distribution is basically an entirely different business to running a digital storefront. "Because we are talking about physical media, we need to think about logistics, we need to think about storage," Paczynski said, adding that it's "a very, very complicated thing." But the idea has been on the company's collective mind "for years now," so he's not ruling it out.
If you don't want to wait, there's always projects like Big Box Collection that let you print your own facsimiles. Or buy used! A few scratches and a giant sticker reading "PROPERTY OF TREVOR" just lends character, right?

title: Grand Theft Auto 6 teased a handful of its upcoming radio stations and its music curation is as strong as ever
author: Mollie Taylor
text:
Grand Theft Auto's radio stations have long stood as an integral part of the series' whole vibe—either offering time capsules of the times each game was set in (Vice City), or offering a realistic blend of classic and modernity a la Grand Theft Auto 5's excellent music curation.
Critical Hit
(Image credit: Future) Welcome to Critical Hit , where I (or someone else on the PC Gamer team) celebrate and lament all things videogame music, audio design, and the ways our favourite games make our ears tingle.
I've been just a tad giddy to discover what awaits me in Grand Theft Auto 6's car stereos when the game launches on November 19, which has me surprised that Rockstar teasing six of its upcoming stations earlier this month completely flew under my radar.
Well, now I've had a gander and listened to all 12 minutes of its DJs bantering and a peppering of bangers between. And I gotta say, I'm already jazzed to speed down Leonida's highways with some of these stations at full volume.
Rockstar's licensed music curation rarely misses, and that very much seems to be the continuing trend with Grand Theft Auto 6. While we don't know just how many radio stations there are in total yet—this is the first game where we'll be able to tune in to both terrestrial music stations and podcasts, it being 2026 and all—but the six that were teased were the exact kind of flavours I've come to expect from the series.
(Image credit: Rockstar Games) There's Latin station Cocoteo FM, classic country Back Country Radio, African channel AfroBANK FM, all-out metal hub The Chamber 106.6, pop banger central Flash FM, and hip-hop destination Dirty South Classics. I'm already 100% here for The Chamber's setlist, being an elder emo and all, with bands like Black Sabbath, Pantera, and Slayer making their way onto Leonida's airwaves. But I'm also jazzed to see newer blood on the scene, like Bad Bunny's appearance on Cocoteo.
My biggest interest was in Flash FM, though. Non-Stop Pop has become such an iconic radio station for me, thanks to some excellent song choices and Cara Delevigne's delightfully deadpan delivery. It doesn't seem like I'm going to be disappointed, though—Alex Consani takes up the mantle as model-turned-radio-host alongside the excellent artist Robyn (of Bulletproof fame), and hearing one of my favourite songs in MGMT's Electric Feel is all the confidence I need in Rockstar's keen ear.
While the previews do show criminally little interactions between the hosts (it seems like Grand Theft Auto 6 is going for duos across all its stations, presumably for some easy back-and-forth banter), I'm sure there'll still be satire in droves to come.

title: Jagex partnered with a RuneScape-inspired idle game to turn the sequel into an official spinoff
author: Justin Wagner
text:
It's easy to knock old-school RPGs, especially grindfests like RuneScape, for being games where you endlessly and sometimes mindlessly make numbers go up. But Melvor Idle, which self-bills as a RuneScape-inspired idle adventure game that claims to squeeze the genre into its "purest form," leans into that—and Jagex has partnered with developer Games by Malcs to make the RuneScape connection official.
The announcement blog from Jagex reads, "Melvor Idle takes a lot of inspiration from RuneScape and you can just feel it," adding that Jagex's support (and branding) is intended to help make the game "even bigger … while Melvor Idle 2 doesn’t take place in Gielinor, we think a fan-built idle game inspired by our MMOs is more than worthy of the title."
This isn't the first time Jagex has collaborated with Games by Malcs. It became the first Melvor Idle's publisher five years ago, albeit without a branding tweak. While RuneScape has had its fair share of monetization controversies over the years (you can see just how skeptical people were of the partnership when it was first announced on Reddit ), it doesn't seem like Melvor has been compromised by trouble along those lines—the announcement blog proudly proclaims the sequel will have "no microtransactions."
Beyond that, it seems like a bigger version of the familiar idle RPG with overhauled visuals and a higher level cap of 120. You might find it a bit odd that it's a "RuneScape Adventure" that doesn't take place in the MMO's setting, but I'm not sure how many people are really invested in Jagex's games for the scintillating lore and worldbuilding. If you end up feeling like a stranger in a strange land, you can always hire someone to spam "buying gf" in a chat window while you get your idle on.

title: Here's one bit of good news for Mass Effect: modders are bringing the multiplayer mode to Mass Effect Legendary Edition
author: Jody Macgregor
text:
When Mass Effect 3's beloved multiplayer mode was left out of the Legendary Edition, there was much wailing and gnashing of teeth. Redemption has finally come in the form of the ME3Tweaks modding team, who have spent the last three years quietly working to not only get multiplayer working, but improve it.
"It's not just a ME3MP port but rather an extensive remaster of the experience," says modder Audemus. "This includes new features like bringing forward LE's native features like controller support/HDR, overhauled UI, rebaked level lighting, upscaled/redrawn textures, upgraded shaders, improved networking/server replication, extensive bug fixes, new gameplay modes, and a stable format for future mod support and easy installation/compatibility."
They're even adding new game modes, like one called "Unified" that combines enemies from multiple factions, and letting players either join ME3Tweaks' server, or set up their own private servers.
The ME3Tweaks team are the same modders who previously revived and revised the Pinnacle Station expansion , a lost DLC for the original Mass Effect that was also left out of the Legendary Edition. They're planning to release the multiplayer mod on N7 Day, which is also when composer Sam Hulick plans to release a re-scored version of the leaked Mass Effect Universe trailer .

title: Obsidian's Josh Sawyer on RPG cities: 'Compared to a dungeon, generally speaking, a town is 4x the expense per square foot'
author: Ted Litchfield
text:
In a new Q&A vlog on his YouTube channel, Obsidian studio design director Josh Sawyer took a question about why there are so few RPGs in contemporary urban settings. Part of the problem, according to Sawyer: They're more difficult and costly to make than other RPG environments.
Elsewhere in this section, Sawyer cited Baldur's Gate 2's Athkatla, Disco Elysium, and the recent Zero Parades as RPGs that land the plane on believable, dense urban environments⁠—though Sawyer notes that the latter two have the advantage of not needing to work in as many believable combat encounters as other RPGs.
A few others spring to mind for me: Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines, Cyberpunk 2077, and Baldur's Gate 3's version of the titular city. But all of those really highlight Sawyer's point about expense and challenge. Vampire and Cyberpunk were notoriously difficult development cycles for their respective studios. I'll always be a BG3 Act 3 defender, but it's definitely the part of the game with the most noticeable seams.
But even if they're hard to make, I love urban adventures in RPGs, whether as part or the whole of a game. Novigrad and Oxenfurt are two of my favorite parts of The Witcher 3, for example. For a real niche example of an urban RPG you should have on your radar, I highly recommend the early access Moves of the Diamond Hand .

title: Footage of what sure looks like a Persona 1 remake has leaked
author: Jody Macgregor
text:
Persona tragics have been begging for remakes of the first two games in the series for ages (at least, the ones who aren't begging for remakes of the PS2-era Shin Megami Tensei games instead). After thoroughly milking Persona 4 and 5, series producer Kazuhisa Wada said in August , "personally, I think it's something we should definitely do."
Now, almost two minutes of footage from what sure looks like a Persona 1 remake has leaked via the GamingLeaksAndRumours subreddit . It shows some dungeon exploration, typically flashy combat, and a dialogue scene all in the modern Persona style.
Oddly, Tatsuya from Persona 2 is one of the party members, though it's possible this is a cross-promotional skin you can equip. Or maybe the remakes will incorporate some kind of Persona Q-style crossover?
While it's fair to be suspicious this could be AI-generated footage, it seems both a bit too long and too internally consistent for that to be the case. And it's not like Atlus hasn't got form, given that we found out the Persona 3 remake was real via a leak as well.

title: The HeroQuest board game is coming to Steam with a quest editor and multiplayer
author: Jody Macgregor
text:
Avalon Hill's deluxe rerelease of the classic dungeon crawl board game HeroQuest is getting a digital edition courtesy of Nomad Games, who previously adapted board games like Talisman, Love Letter, and Fury of Dracula. Expect goblin-bashing, trap-disarming, treasure-hunting, and spell-casting. I'll use my broadsword.
As well as solo play, with the computer taking on the role of the Evil Wizard and his minions, it'll support online multiplayer with up to four players as the heroes, and a fifth optionally taking over as the villainous Zargon. (It's based on the American version, so no Morcar here.)
The most promising detail revealed so far is the inclusion of a quest editor so players can create their own maps and missions, as well as downloading quests made by others through mod.io integration.
Hopefully it includes the rules additions from HeroQuest First Light , especially the option to just move eight squares per turn instead of rolling to move if there aren't any monsters on the board. Slogging across the dungeon to get back to the exit 2d6 squares at a time is a real chore otherwise.
HeroQuest: Digital Edition is scheduled for release on Steam in 2027, with a closed beta playtest coming soon.

title: Valve's Steam Frame has taken a spot in the top ten most popular VR headsets on Steam
author: James Bentley
text:
Valve's second mighty expensive, yet mighty impressive VR headset, the Steam Frame , launched in the latter half of September, meaning October was the first full month where players could actually use it. The latest Steam Hardware Survey suggests a rather big bump in usage for Valve's VR headset this past month.
In September, the Steam Frame accounted for just 0.41% of VR headset usage. In October, that number jumped to 4.13%. That means it surpassed the Oculus Rift S, Sony PS VR2, HTC Vive, Windows Mixed Reality (which is a platform, as opposed to a single headset), the first Oculus Rift and Bigscreen Beyond. It is now the sixth most popular VR headset, sitting just .37% behind the Pico 4, and a hefty 24.14% behind the Meta Quest 3.
The 3.72% increase for the Steam Frame is the biggest jump upwards in October, and the biggest tumble was taken by the Oculus Quest 2, which lost 3.57%.
The Steam Frame officially released on September 18, with preorders going live on September 14, but that doesn't mean buyers got their hands on the headset on the day it went live. So the bump can not only be partially attributed to continued sales over October, but also to shipping times.
It's also worth noting that both the 256 GB and 1 TB models are backordered, meaning even if you sign up for one now, you will simply be put on a waiting list. That means Frame usage is unlikely to entirely stagnate from here.

Given the Steam Frame has enjoyed such a large bump even with customers struggling to get their hands on the headset, this suggests the VR market on Steam isn't huge. Though it is worth taking these stats with a pinch of salt.
The Steam Hardware Survey is an opt-in survey Valve takes every month. This means it only looks at a fraction of Steam users to get general statistics. This is why stats tend to change a tad each month. For instance, the Nvidia GeForce RTX 3060 is currently the most popular graphics card in the survey, but it saw a 0.08% increase last month. The RTX 4060 saw a downward shift of 0.40%, pushing it below the RTX 3060.
As such, the Hardware Survey can only ever give a rough reading of usage each month, but it still seems like a good sign for Valve's latest bit of hardware.

title: Arc Raiders devs used a music sample 'from a piano in Chernobyl' that someone had discovered in the Forbidden Zone
author: Elie Gould
text:
Arc Raiders has a terrific soundscape, although it can sometimes be hard to hear it when you're getting hunted down by your fellow players or bloodthirsty arcs. The game is quite quiet, aside from the occasional sound of distant gunfire, the clicks and cracks from small roaming arcs, and the noise of shuffling scrap as raiders sort through abandoned buildings for valuable items. But perhaps the best noise in all of Arc Raiders comes from the few instruments raiders can find amid the rubble.
"One of the gameplay designers, really early on, made a trumpet," Pajor says. "And it was so out of place, and we were like 'why are we making it?'" The musical items in Arc Raiders serve multiple purposes. There's the social incentive to play an instrument, to bond with strangers and just show them that you're a harmless, relatively chill dude. But there's also the strategic purpose of using noises to lure arcs. Perhaps you're herding them into a trap or ambush or maybe you're trying to distract the aggro of one arc away from another vulnerable player.
Avid players of Arc Raiders will notice, however, that there's no trumpet available in game. Well that's because the trumpet eventually became what we now know as the lure grenade. Apparently a playable trumpet was just too silly to the devs at first, so they settled on something a bit more useful. But now, over a year later from launch players can enjoy multiple instruments like the piano, guitar, harmonica, flute, banjo, recorder, and the trusty shaker.
"It's been almost seven years of exploring this world. [Composers Patrik Andrén and Johan Söderqvist] used to be performing musicians before they became composers so they have a lot of friends who are Sweden's best jazz musicians," Pajor adds. Aside from the Chernobyl piano, which is certainly one of the stranger sources of music I've heard of, composers Andrén and Söderqvist are also known for their abstract use of everyday items to make music and noises.
A lot of raw synthesisers are used to create arc-adjacent noises, but they've also hooked up different kinds of fruits to a synthesiser to grab some slightly weirder sounds. title: Ray tracing memory usage could be reduced by up to 90% thanks to 'most significant' DirectX update
author: Jess Kinghorn
text:
While I go 'oo' at every perfectly lit videogame vista, ray tracing can sometimes make my gaming rig go 'HNNNG'. I love a traced ray as much as the next person, but realistic reflections and lighting can be a bit of a memory hog. Thankfully, Microsoft is previewing something new for DirectX that could significantly take the load off many ageing rigs.
It's a pair of features called 'Clustered Geometry' and 'Partitioned TLAS'. At the risk of oversimplifying, you can think of this DirectX update as bringing tech very similar to Nvidia RTX Mega Geometry to every other GPU vendor.
Obviously there's more to it than that, though, with Microsoft describing this as the " most significant update [to DXR] since its debut in 2018 ." Top line: Microsoft's own testing of this update suggests it could reduce ray tracing memory load by as much as 90% without the need for a team green GPU (via Techspot ).
So, how does it work? Well, without this update, ray tracing is already beaming between less detailed versions of the geometry you see in-game. Traditional ray tracing tech does this because bouncing around detailed models afresh for every frame would simply take too long.
Clustered geometry slices up the detailed models into neat little packages of 256 triangles or fewer. Partitioned TLAS then does a similar thing for the entire videogame vista, splitting a scene into smaller regions. Why? Well, rather than searching the entire map every time, looking for what's changed and updating the frame accordingly, the ol' dread pirate Ray Tracing needs only to run their finger over the quadrants they know are different, marking the spot with 'X'—or something like that, the metaphor got away from me a bit in the middle there.
(Image credit: Asus) Basically, this fresh DirectX tech massively simplifies the ray tracing data your rig has to check and update frame to frame. That could free up a whole lotta memory, with Microsoft demonstrating a reduction of 7.5 GB to 774 MB on an AMD Radeon RX 9070 . Obviously, frame rates also benefitted, jumping from a wince-worthy 1.2 fps to a very impressive 79 fps in Microsoft's testing.
Now, this isn't really a case of simply installing an update and, 'whee, you're flying!' Microsoft issues a fair few caveats—for one thing, not all games are going to replicate the wins its specialised test environment saw.
For another, working with clustered geometry and all of those packages of up to 256 triangles uses a lot more temporary scratch memory compared to traditional tech—that presents its own logistical concerns for game developers.
It's also worth reiterating that this update is not yet widely available, and there's no word yet on when PC gamers like you and me will be able to get our mitts on it either. If you feel like going sicko mode, though, Microsoft writes you can gain access to experimental features like this by using "matching Agility SDK preview headers and runtime, a supporting driver, and Windows Developer Mode."
Still, the potential to cut down memory usage without needing to buy any new hardware is very promising during these times of runaway pricing for both memory and GPUs . If I can put off a pricey upgrade for a few years more, I'll be happy.

title: After 500 hours in Monster Train 2, its final faction of bondage angels is teaching me new ways to win
author: Evan Lahti
text:
Their aesthetic? Chains, whips; spiked. Their mood? Afflicted, condemned, ritualistic. Their angels? Dark. Their maiden? Iron.
Friendship ended with dwarven gearsmiths ; my new favorite clan in Monster Train 2 is the tortured edgelords.
The final faction being added to Monster Train 2, The Punished, arrive November 10 as a paid DLC. Their theme is self-damage, with new keywords and spells that, primarily, reward power in exchange for hurting yourself. Your pain? Enemies' bane.
Leaving a mark
Though existing MT2 clans like the Melting Remnant revolve around forms of sacrifice, The Punished are absolutely thirsty for it. They bring new keywords like Chained (enemy units take half the damage that your units take) that make damage an active solution to enemy waves. The self-flagellation angle likewise brings new purpose to some existing spells and equipment, and jives great with partner clans that provide protection from pain (Lazarus League) or more ways to inflict it (Pyreborne).
Damaging my own guys sounds like a risk-reward tactic that requires sophisticated play. In my first run as The Punished, I anticipated having to do brain-wracking calculus about how much damage to absorb. But instead, I've found the new clan to be one of the most powerful and, at least with one of their champions, easy to play.
A lot of that is down to the utility of their new gimmick, a big purple gem called the Monolith . Here's a breakdown of what makes it special:
Their clan mechanic, the Monolith, sacrifices cards from your hand. Sacrificing a card grants 1 Devotion, a bar that you fill across the run to level up your Monolith level.
1 Monolith level = 1 Zeal. Zeal is +1 attack, +1 max HP when you deploy a unit. There's no cap on Monolith level, but in my best runs I was able to achieve 10 or 11.
Curses can be sacrificed to the Monolith like any other card. So if you have 2 Curses of Entropy in your hand while facing the Titans, but you have 2 energy, you can just click the Monolith twice to vaporize them, avoiding their debuffs completely. Extremely helpful.
One of the more fun strategies I stumbled on is playing curse roulette with this system, hoping that a Monolith click deletes the undesired card in your hand.
Also, sacrificing a card to the Monolith triggers Offering (if discarded, play that card)
"Level up the Monolith by sacrificing cards to earn Devotion, which grants Zeal, which buffs attack and HP for all units" kind of sounds like a line from a ProZD deckbuilder parody video (I will take any opportunity to reference the legendary Dairy Cow combo ), but it's really not complicated. Click the purple crystal, make cards go away, permascale a little bit.
Though it can change the calculus for a few units, Zeal isn't that game-breaking on its own: usually you're just increasing the ceiling of a unit's HP to set up cards like Zealot's Halo, an equipment that gives +1 attack for every 1 HP you're missing.
More potent is The Punished's starter champion, Archus, an S-tier champ that amps damage based on lost HP, but has the versatility to debuff enemy damage as well. All of his build paths grant him Flight. His best variant deploys a "Darkshard" into the lane he flies into, a 0-attack artifact that does one of the following, on your choice:
Blinding Darkshard: Give enemy units -3 (scaling to -7 on max level)
Looming Darkshard: Apply Bloodshed (+1 to all friendly units on the floor when a friendly unit takes damage—scaling all the way to +3)
Shattering Darkshard: Sacrifice the Darkshard to deal 40 damage (300 damage on max level)
Bloodshed is really, really powerful with the right unit pairings and a cheap spell or two that hurts yourself. What's wild is that Archus can deploy a Darkshard in every lane, with a cooldown of 2 on his flight ability. I might anticipate a nerf on that. Scaling your whole floor from received hits (including self-targeted spells!) is a wonderful way to accelerate sweepers or backline bruisers. Archus good.
Scarred Justicar, the second friendly unit from the middle, gets +15 attack when hit by a friendly spell or ability. Here I've slapped him up to 510x2, helped by a pile of Zeal on every unit on my floor. (Image credit: Shiny Shoe) Chain pain
Zariel, the other champ, is more advanced. The first angel cast out of heaven, "Zariel has been imprisoned for so long that her original crime has been forgotten to time." Sick. Although, you'd think that that would enable some kind of clemency?
Since her arms and wings are bound in chains, Zariel has no base attack. What she does have are three diverse paths that all play off sponging up as much damage as possible:
Matriarch of Chains: Apply Chained 1 to enemies on turn start
Pain Maiden: Ability - Paintouch: Deal 3 damage to an enemy unit per stack of Pain (starts with 10 Pain, gains Pain for every point of damage taken by friendly units)
Devout: Siphon - Gain 1 Devotion. Incant - Deal 6 damage to the front enemy unit, increased by 6 per Monolith level
I asked Shiny Shoe CEO Mark Cooke what combos the studio has found useful with Zariel. "A lot of Hellhorned cards like Branding Rite, Dark Deal, and Inferno work really well with Zariel's Pain and Chain paths. Pox is a great spell for consistent friendly damage, because it applies Decay 10 to all units," says Cooke. "Zariel's Pain Maiden path especially synergizes well with The Condemned, because the unit has Tenacious, it won't die to any friendly damage and it even amplifies the damage it takes and redirects it to an enemy, so it's great for pinging and stacking Pain while still killing enemies."
On my second run with Zariel, in the final rounds of a battle, I was dealing 1000 damage from her Paintouch ability, and I was doing it each turn because the ability has a cooldown of 1. On a couple other attempts, I couldn't create damage outputting units to pair with her quickly enough, and my run collapsed.
The superstar of the roster might be Penitent Sentinel, an uncommon tank that becomes MT2's most durable frontliner.
This is one of the few weaknesses of The Punished—although several units have good base attack, instantaneous damage can be hard to acquire. Reaper of Suffering, The Punished's only sweeper, starts with a generous 60 attack (as much as Demon Fiend, a 4-cost Hellhorned unit), but it also starts Suppressed (meaning she cannot attack), needing a cooldown of 4 to expire before she emerges from that state. Taking damage decreases that cooldown, and incredibly, she heals to full HP when she emerges from Supressed and gains flight when you cross that threshold.
This isn't the only star unit on The Punished. Forsaken Berserker gains one multistrike for every two Monolith levels. Scarred Justicar, an uncommon, ended up being my damage solution on several runs. He simply gains +15 attack when hit by a friendly spell or ability, and considering one of the starter cards deals a gentle 2 damage, you can gain perhaps +30 or +45 attack in a round between spells and other effects. Slap a stack of multistrike and the new 3-cost equipment Sineater on him (Deal 8 damage to self, attack immediately, cooldown 2), and you have a high damage solution that just takes a little time to set up.
The superstar of the roster, though, might be Penitent Sentinel, an uncommon tank that becomes MT2's most durable frontliner if you're able to draft it early. This stoic statue unit cannot be healed, but it gains +1 HP on revenge, astoundingly rare health permascaling that is set-and-forget simple. I found myself taking the "enemies gain multistrike" trial just to welcome more attacks against Penitent Sentinel. In some runs I was ending with nearly 300 HP, linked to a Titanite upgrade that effectively doubled that. Wild.
Punished Spike goes huge with cards that generate energy (like Trial By Fire). (Image credit: Shiny Shoe) Riding the pain train
After 12 wins with The Punished, I love that they have several viable units to pick from, and how much they synergize with a variety of clans. I kept finding new ways of winning with Zariel, and my strangest victory was with this configuration:
The Punished (Zariel) + Underlegion secondary clan, facing Savagery
No real tank unit, no sweep! 😬
But I have Remnant Pact to grant Endless to Chainbearer, with a reasonable-ish 80 HP (Largestone/Smidgestone)
Zariel does 96 damage to the front enemy on Incant
Zariel applies Chained 1 to enemies on turn start + Dungeon Mooring artifact stacks an additional 1 Chained, so enemies on the first floor take 1X the damage that my units take. But I didn't have any massive self-damage spells. In some cases though this was enough incoming damage on my units to kill the backline enemy sweeper units based on the damage I took from the enemy frontline units.
In other words: You hurt me so much that you hurt your own guys enough to kill them, who otherwise would have killed me. Congrats, you played yourself?
Manifold Mirror + Mushy Room to sap every floor, which somehow didn't anti-synergy with Chained
Use spells to damage my own Scarred Justicar, who I gave multistrike, to attain something like 150-260x2 damage
Punished Spike with remove consume enchantment, played on Scarred Justicar (often granting 56 Zeal, which is +56 attack and +56 max HP)
In a couple of situations I played the equipment Shackles of Spite (this unit does 2X damage if their HP is ≤50%) on Scarred Justicar to boost their attack to ~425x2, but I didn't pull this off consistently
Two 1-cost Rots for some extra damage on bosses
11 Monolith level, mostly from Zariel
I had no plan and was mostly freestyling through this, my upgrade selections weren't particularly strong. I was surprised to beat Savagery, let alone the Titans.
After 500 hours in Monster Train 2, it's refreshing to beat the game in an unexpected way. I truly thought this run was doomed because I had little traditional damage, no sweep, no tank, and no decapitating spells.
Despite modest attack power here, Penitent Sentinel buys me enough time to win this fight. (Image credit: Shiny Shoe) The Punished's masochistic theme works. And Shiny Shoe's treatment of these tortured angels is nice (their Carolina Panthers-blue skin helps them stand out, even among the pale blue Melting Remnant), though their stoic reverence doesn't leave a lot of room for quirk.
I would've loved to have seen a silly torture sicko among the roster, but I'll settle for Lasher, the first backline unit that hits any friendly units positioned in front of him for 1 damage (I don't recommend relying on Damage Shield when he's on the floor). Just think of it as giving your guys a helpful, spiked-chain pat on the back.
It's appropriate for the final update to a game I like a lot to hurt a little. But Shiny Shoe CEO Mark Cooke did indicate that the studio may not be done with the franchise. "At this time The Punished is the last DLC planned for MT2," Cooke told me. "However, we love the world of Monster Train, and hope to work on more Monster Train games in the future!"

"At this time The Punished is the last DLC planned for MT2," Cooke told me. "However, we love the world of Monster Train, and hope to work on more Monster Train games in the future!"

title: 定档12月14日：这个后来者要做大世界二游的“第一个”
text:
乐元素 《白银之城》 宣布定档12月14日上线。
看到这个日期， 游戏日报 特意去翻了翻它的历程。今年年初《白银之城》开启首测；半年后7月进行二测，地图扩展到首测的数倍，一口气放出前四章主线；10月份不久前刚开启保密付费测；紧接着就直接公测定档。10个月，在一年内完成三轮测试，然后直接上线，这样的效率在一众开放世界二游中相当少见。
近年来我们也看过太多的大世界项目，产品首测之后磨上两三年，是常规操作，甚至测到一半推倒重来，上线日期一推再推的戏码也看过太多回。但《白银之城》这一路却几乎没什么多余的动作，透露着胸有成竹的感觉。这就让人好奇，它的底气从何而来？
从 游戏日报 体验过的多次测试来看，维多利亚时代背景，英伦风格以及 二游少见的侦探题材 ，都只是表相。这位后来居上的开放世界二游真正押注的，是二游用户在体验上越来越渴望的方向：由看戏的人，变成戏里的人。而《白银之城》想成为的正是这样的“第一款”。
“下一代”的新风向
过去几年，二游剧情演出品质的迭代升级，大伙都有目共睹，越来越多作品开始追求电影级别的视听表现，也由此诞生了不少令玩家津津乐道的出圈名场面。但在演出品质不断拔高的同时，二游的剧情体验却始终存在着一个难以回避的问题：故事越来越好看了，玩家却并不一定真正参与到了故事其中。
这几年， 我们总能看到有玩家开玩笑说自己在剧情里活像个摄像头，无论是否认同剧情人物的行为、是否满足故事的发展方向，能做的却往往只有点点鼠标，播放下一段演出，等待故事的推进。 这固然能带来连贯完整的叙事体验，但如今，玩家已逐渐不甘于只做故事的看客，而希望追求更高层次、更贴近故事情节的体验视角，需求上已不可同日而语。
放到品类层面，在游戏日报看来，目前二游大世界的竞争有两条明确的主线：一条是内容，一条是玩法。尤其在内容这条线上，头部产品已经将演出观感卷到了相当高的水准，玩家对于“好看”的阈值也被反复抬高，单纯提升视听表现所带来的边际收益正在递减。当越来越多的产品都能拿出电影级的剧情演出时，演出品质便不再是足以支撑产品突围的差异点，甚至已经成为了下一代二游的入场门槛。
与此同时，大世界品类本身的特性，又进一步放大了传统剧情体验中的矛盾。玩家在开放世界中能够自由探索、战斗，以自己的方式与世界发生联系，可在主线剧情当中，玩家接收信息、阅读世界的方式又往往是被动的，只能停下脚步等待真相的解明。玩法层面越是强调自由，剧情层面的这种被动感便越显突兀。
照此说来，内容侧的竞争已经卷到头了？ 事实则并非如此，当演出品质的竞争逐渐触及边际收益的瓶颈，下一阶段的竞争便开始转向一个新的维度：玩家的“亲身参与感”。
比起继续追求如何把故事讲得更加精彩，厂商开始思考如何改变玩家与故事之间的关系，让玩家亲自入戏。这里的关键也不只是增加几次交互、提供几个对话选项，而是让玩家的行动与判断真正成为剧情体验的一部分，从单纯接收故事，转向亲身经历乃至推动故事。
下一代二游内容的竞争力，正在从讲得好转向让你在场。这并不意味着演出品质不再重要，而是说，在让玩家看见一个精彩的故事之后，如何让他们真正成为故事的一部分，正在成为新的差异化竞争方向——《白银之城》则恰好踩在这条线上，它要做落地的“第一款”。
《白银之城》给予了玩家一个更为专业的身份：有阅历、知识渊博的侦探，让玩家作为白银城前精英探员重回故地，不再是被不断灌输的世界观的外来者，需要依靠调查、取证、问询、推理，一步步把故事走出来，自己决定要经历一段怎样的故事。这一设计的特别之处在于，侦探身份并非只是主角人设上的一层包装，而是成为了玩家实际参与剧情的手段。
换言之，《白银之城》希望建立的，不只是让玩家“看见”一个精彩故事的沉浸感，更是让玩家通过实际行动，感受到自己正在亲手推动故事的发展。相比于被动接受一段预先安排好的剧情，这种由玩家自身的调查、思考与判断所构成的经历，显然更容易建立起一种真正置身其中的参与感。
这又说回了前面提到的“摄像头”问题。过去不少二游始终在想方设法提高这台摄像头的画质、运镜与表现力，却很少考虑过为什么玩家一定要被固定在这个机位上。而《白银之城》想做的，恰恰是把摄像头从支架上拧下来，塞到玩家自己手里，在原先的剧情体验基础上更进一步。
该“观众”登台了
那么《白银之城》是怎么让玩家亲自登上舞台的？
首先是讲故事的方式。主流二游的故事信息基本都是系统直接灌输给玩家，播一段过场动画或者其他角色交流中直接表达，答案就到手里了，玩家们只需要在一旁看着等待。以侦探玩法为重点的《白银之城》，把这个顺序整个倒了过来。
游戏里用得最多的功能，是观察。抵达一处现场，周围环境、当事人身上，到处都是能查的点，主角看到了什么、心里在想什么，都被客观描述出来，让玩家自己思考。甚至游戏中每次见到新的角色，玩家都可以对角色进行观察，收集线索。比如寻找助手那段戏码，冒冒失失的阿芙连泡茶都不会，通过观察可以看出她双手光洁，反应釜也没用过，观察结果和她的生手身份对得上，说明人虽然冒失，话倒没撒谎。
还有一段去警察局找证物的剧情，由于证物被锁进了保险箱，玩家需要先观察现场，再进行简单的推理解谜才能开箱。只是个小小的细节，但给玩家一种这东西不是剧情发我的，是我自己找到的成就感。
只有在玩家侦查到了足够多的线索，收集了足够的人物关系、证物、证词，试着推出结论后，才能推进故事的发展，玩家不再仅仅等待故事给出下一个答案，而是在主动寻找答案的过程中，逐步建立对事件的理解，成为推动故事的动力。
同时，这样的设计和体验并不会重度和烧脑。
此前多次测试体验下来并不难，观察、检查现场、问询、在线索板上整理、进思维空间重演，说起来复杂，但每一步单拎出来都不硬核，压根没打算把玩家拦在剧情门口。比如问询这个环节，让周围人了解情况时，对话里有些关键选项在调查完成前是锁着的，等相关线索查出来，它才会亮起来，等于游戏在帮你兜着节奏，不会出现手里没东西却硬要推理的迷惑场面。
观察同样如此，现场能查看的点会有提示，走过去点一下，主角看到了什么、怎么判断，直接打在屏幕上。游戏中的角色包括主角自己，会在每次收集线索时给出适度的提示，帮助玩家分析推理，不怕走进死胡同。
最有意思的事，哪怕《白银之城》在逻辑上没给玩家出难题，但给人的感觉却很到位。现场是玩家亲自一寸寸看过的，证词和证物是玩家亲手钉到线索板上的，非常有我在破案的感觉，能让玩家觉得不是看一个侦探在破案，相反自己就是那个侦探。
这样的分寸明显是刻意设计的，主线承担的是让所有人都能顺顺当当走下去，所以不卡人，不设答错就推进不下去的门槛，部分玩家想挑战的可能想错、可能漏线索的烧脑推理乐趣，被挪到了奇案推演玩法里。
比如二测中的“死体苏生之谜”。案子从主角的老朋友法索医生说起，一位老患者突然离世，死因据说是因为心脏病，但法索医生对此保持怀疑，并无意间发现了患者手臂上有外伤，而主角与法索医生在患者下葬后再次探查，却发现手臂上的外伤消失了，再加上现场的疑点重重，甚至传出了吸血鬼的说法。
整个案件调查过程如同传统的侦探小说，玩家要先在现场仔细翻找，所有线索都得自己收集，再把拿到的证物和证词钉到线索板上，试着拼出因果。哪些是真线索，哪些是故意放出来干扰的，哪些话听着合理、细想全是窟窿，游戏不替你分辨，都要靠玩家自己动脑思索。这起案件一共有三个结局，区别在于玩家最终认定谁是凶手。
《白银之城》不告诉玩家标准答案，或许玩家在调查过程中会被带偏，或许会采纳错误的证词，也可以把一个看着严丝合缝的推论定案，在结局里眼睁睁看它结出什么果。在测试期间，引起社区中不少玩家的讨论，有玩家提到在前中段都以为自己摸到真相了，甚至真信了吸血鬼那套，直到结论揭晓才发现想错了，体会到了极大的惊喜。过程由玩家上手，结果由玩家来判断，身临其境的体验和最终破案的成就感，已经有了保证。
结语
回过头来看，这一年《白银之城》走得特别踏实。这份从容，大概来自于选对了方向，走在了下一时代的前列。这就是“第一款”的分量，不是第一款侦探题材二游，是第一款把亲身参与做成完整体验的二游大世界。
方向对不对，市场已经给了初步答案，破千万的预约说明《白银之城》的这种体验并不缺受众。12月14日之后，真正的考验才开始，这座维多利亚风格的白银城已经搭好舞台，该让玩家登台了。
